# Simployer One - Recruitment - Connecting Cronofy to Recruitment

Connecting Cronofy to Recruitment

Simployer Recruitment`s interview scheduling allows you to automate the scheduling of interviews, offering candidates a 1-1 interview, either by phone, video or in-person, or supporting panel style interviews with multiple client-side attendees, or sequential interviews where multiple interviewers take part in a single interview stage as different times, eg ‘Hiring Manager A’ doing 30-mins followed by 45-mins with ‘Hiring Manager B’.

The first thing to do to enable automated interview scheduling is to connect to Cronofy, our API which enables us to gather your live calendar availability.

To set this up, head to Settings - Integrations - My Integrations .

Then, find Cronofy and click Connect . You will be prompted to integrate your individual work email account. You will receive a success message, and the button with show as “Disconnect” once the integration is complete.

Note: we do not support integration with shared inboxes through Cronofy as this integration requires a personal calendar to be available to select slots from.

Note : If your company uses Microsoft for business, the highest likelihood is that you have Microsoft 365 – please ensure you select Office 365 from the Cronofy options, not Outlook.com, for example.

Once you have integrated your calendar, you can set your availability for interviews  by going to Settings – Personal – My Preferences. Here you can select your date format, time zone and the days and hours that you wish to be available for interview, in conjunction with your live calendar availability

What does the ‘candidate match score threshold’ mean when I’m creating a new job? When setting up a job, you can determine the % match you deem a good threshold to be a match with your job. This will enable you to pull candidates from your candidate database who are above that threshold into the ‘sourced’ column, giving you a way to regenerate your database and have warmer candidates to reach out to. The sourced candidates from the database will only be added to your pipeline for a job on your request, so you don’t need to worry about this feature if you only want to invite new applicants to apply for the job, rather than to see if there are any matching candidates in your database already. You can set that % on job setup, but nothing further will happen unless action is taken from the job kanban. Why does a candidate have a score out of 5 on the kanban rather than candidate match score? Scorecards , which are filled in by interviewers once they have interviewed a candidate, will take precedence over the candidate match score, although the candidates match score will still appear on the candidate profile underneath the candidate name, should you wish to review it at a later date. # Simployer One - Recruitment - Integrating job boards

Integrating job boards with Recruitment

At the final stage of creating a job – Sharing – you can also choose to publish the job on a number of job boards.  Currently, you can automatically post your advert to any of the free job sites we are directly integrated with - Adzuna, Jooble, CareerJet and Google Jobs.

Simply toggle on any of the free job boards where you would like your advert to appear:

The advert will then automatically pushed through XML feed to be posted on the job site, and your applicants will appear under Applied in your job kanban, tracked through to the job board where they arrived. Only Account Owners and Admins can do this for every role, while Job owners can only do this for roles they own.

Note: Once you've toggled these on, it is down to the job board to 'scrape' for new jobs and add to their sites when found. Each job board will 'scrape' at different times, and Recruitment doesn't control this. Generally, it takes 24-72h for the jobs to be posted on the free job boards after they have been added, but this can vary.

Closing a job advert

To close an advert from one of these sites, go to Jobs and select the three dots to the right of the job in question. Select “Edit” from and then confirm, then select “Sharing” to get through to the Job Sharing page, where you will be able to disable the toggles and save.

Note: The jobs will not be immediately taken down from these boards but will be removed from the next 'scrape' for jobs which is usually within 24 hours depending on the provider.

# Simployer One - Recruitment - Linkedin

How to post your jobs to LinkedIn with Simployer Recruitment

There are three ways you can share your job to LinkedIn through Recruitment: LinkedIn company feed post, basic adverts (which are free) or paid adverts.

Note: Depending on your LinkedIn plan, there may be costs associated with adding jobs to your company page - this is something you will be able to handle and manage with LinkedIn and not with Recruitment .

LinkedIn free job posting

To connect your company LinkedIn page, head to Settings - Integrations - Company Integrations .

Select LinkedIn Jobs Basic in the pop up, and input your Company ID. Your LinkedIn Company ID is a string of numbers, usually 6 to 9 digits long, that is unique to your company. The guide here explains where to find this code.

You will then be able to post your jobs to LinkedIn from the Sharing stage of job set up - simply toggle on InJobs under Free Job Boards .

LinkedIn paid job posting

To connect your company LinkedIn page, head to Settings - Integrations - Company Integrations .

Select LinkedIn Jobs Premium in the pop up, and input your Company ID. Your LinkedIn Company ID is a string of numbers, usually 6 to 9 digits long, that is unique to your company.

Once your Company ID is entered, click connect an account to authenticate your account and verify your Contract ID (this field will auto-populate).

You will then be able to post your jobs to LinkedIn from the Sharing stage of job set up - simply toggle on InJobs under Paid Job Boards .

Sharing to your LinkedIn company feed

If you're the Recruitment Account Owner or an Admin on Recruitment , you can set up a company-level integration with LinkedIn which will enable you to post jobs from your company as a feed post.

Note: The person enabling this integration must have admin access for their company LinkedIn account for jobs to post to these pages and set up this integration. If they are an admin for multiple companies, then the job will post from all companies they are an admin for so we recommend checking this before you go ahead.

To set up this integration, head to Settings - Integrations - Company Integrations . Next to LinkedIn, there is the option to “Connect”.  You'll then be prompted to sign into your LinkedIn account and Save .

You will then be able to toggle LinkedIn on and off at the Sharing stage of job.

Note: This LinkedIn integration will not post the job onto the company page. If you wish to post a basic job to your company page, please use the LinkedIn free job postings or Premium job postings.

Send and receive emails from a user's email account triggered on Recruitment (via the Recruitment App for Email) Help schedule interviews with access to a user's Team calendar to find available interview slots and schedule meetings (via the Recruitment App for Teams)

Go to Enterprise Applications

Under Security , click on Consent & Permissions In the User Consent Settings section:

Ensure Allow user consent for apps is selected

Return to Enterprise Applications

Click on Admin consent requests under Activity and approve the app

Reconnect the app and you should be good to go!

# Simployer One - Recruitment - Post jobs to Indeed

How to post jobs to Indeed with Recruitment (Indeed sponsored jobs)

Learn how to post your jobs into Indeed and make them available to candidates

Note : After you share your job to your company's Indeed account, you need to sponsor them in order to make them available to candidates. You can read more about sponsored jobs in Indeed on their website .

Connect Simployer Recruitment to Indeed

To connect your company's Indeed page to your Recruitment account, head to Settings - Integrations - Company Integrations and toggle Indeed on.

Type in your company name exactly as it appears in Indeed.

Note: company names are case-sensitive in Indeed.

If you already have an Indeed Campaign, type it here. Otherwise leave it blank and you can always define it later through Indeed.

Post a job to Indeed

Once you have connected Indeed to your Recruitment account, you will be able to post your jobs to Indeed from the Sharing stage of job set up. Simply toggle on Indeed under Paid Job Boards .

After Indeed pulls job posts (every four hours), your jobs will appear on Indeed as flagged. You need to sponsor them to be available to candidates. To do that, you need to go to the campaign tab on Indeed and create a new campaign adding the job that was just transferred.

FAQ

I can not see my job in Indeed, what should I do?

Make sure you have entered the correct company name when you first connected to your Indeed account. Company names are case sensitive in Indeed, use lower and upper case as appears on Indeed. Indeed pulls jobs every 4 hours , make sure you have waited long enough. If the job still does not appear on Indeed, you may need to get in touch with your representative at Indeed . There could be a few reasons for Indeed to not show the job on your account, even though they have it. The transferred job from Indeed only becomes available to candidates after they are sponsored. Make sure you create a campaign for the transferred jobs.

# Simployer One - Recruitment - Creating your career page

Creating your career page

Create and customise your careers page

Recruitment enables you  to create and customise your own careers site in just a few clicks so that you can easily share your job openings, showcase your employer brand and get candidates excited about what your company offers. As an Account Owner or Admin, you can view and edit your careers site by heading to Settings - Career Site - Customise to get started.

When creating and customising your careers site you are able to:

Add your company logo Replace imagery Update your text Add, remove and reorder sections Customise your fonts and colours Add company navigation links

To add your company's logo at the top of your careers page, head to Edit - Upload your new image - Open.

Replacing images

To change the images in your careers page, Edit - Upload your new image - Open.

From here you'll be asked to crop your images to be optimised for both desktop and mobile. You can zoom in and out to get the fit you are looking for.

Note: your images must be less than 5MB.

Updating text

When you begin with customising your careers site, you'll find we've left some placeholder text and best practices you might want to follow, including the Page Title and 'About Us' section. All of these are editable on page, making it simple to adapt to your company messaging.

Adding, removing, and reordering sections

You can add more sections from our templates by heading to Settings - Add a section - Hover over the section and click Add. The newly added section will default to the bottom of the page, but can be adjusted to your desired location.

If you want to change the order of these sections, you can do this by Settings - Reorder page . You can drag and drop to reorder, and use the “trash” icon to remove a section you no longer need.

Changing your fonts and colours

You can update the font, colours, and button styles to match your company's brand and style by heading to Settings - Style .

Updating your navigation links

You can add or edit your company's social media pages (LinkedIn, YouTube, Instagram and more). These can be added under Settings - Navigation Links.

You can also add any additional links you would like in either the header or footer of your career page.

Preview and publish your careers site

When you've added the content of your career page, you can preview it before publishing. To do this, head to Settings in your careers page editor, then Preview .

This will open in a new tab for you to review.

Publishing your careers site

Once you're happy with your preview, you can publish your careers page. To do this, head to Settings in your careers page editor, then Publish . Until you choose to publish the page, it’s not publicly available.

Your career page's URL can be found in Settings - Career Site - Settings - Link to careers page . You can copy this URL to use on your website as a redirect from your “Careers” or “Jobs” page

Integrating with your existing career page

We also offer an API and iFrame giving you flexibility in how you display your live jobs, if you wish to integrate into an existing careers page.

Note: you may need support from an IT contact within your organisation to get this integration up and running.

iFrame integration

The easiest way to integrate is by using the iFrame. Your iFrame code can be found under Settings - Career Site - Settings . This can then be copied, and embedded into your website code base where you would like your vacancies to appear.

This will bring up a box that looks similar to the “jobs” section of the career builder on Candidly, where vacancies you post on Recruitment will be displayed if you select 'Make your job visible' at the Sharing stage of job set up. When a prospective applicant clicks on one of the vacancies, they'll be taken through to the apply page that we host on Recruitment for that job, enabling the candidate to submit their application with ease directly into your kanban for your review.

The text colour used here can be edited at Settings - Company - Profile - Brand Colour

API integration

You can also integrate Recruitment with your career page using our API, which allows for greater customisation of how the jobs appear on your site.

The API key and documentation can be found under Settings - Integrations - Jobs API .

# Simployer One - Recruitment - User roles

User Roles

There are four main permission levels in Recruitment - Account Owner, Admin, User and Reviewer. Account Owners can:

Add and remove other users and determine permission levels (please check the specifics of the integration with the HRIS partner which may impact where user provisioning is selected) Complete the key setup tasks for their account, such as creating the privacy Policy and setting up a career page Access all other product features at Admin-level

Admins can:

Manage all jobs & candidates Customise their careers page View all reports (account-wide) Adjust and manage default templates and create custom templates Manage team and overall agency permissions, as well as company-level integrations

Users can:

Manage jobs they created, including candidates that were involved in them Enable personal profile integrations, but not company level ones View templates and create/edit custom templates Access all other product features at Reviewer-level

Reviewers can:

View jobs that have been assigned to them – they can’t create a job Participate in interviews Fill in scorecards for candidates in jobs they are part of the hiring team for Receive relevant notifications in the Communication Centre (same as all permission levels)

Note: the best way to view this is that admins have full visibility of everything across all users, users have full visibility for all jobs they are involved in, and reviewer level have the lowest permission, only being able to respond to actions required within the jobs they are added to the hiring team for – eg. completing a scorecard or leaving a note against a candidate
